<h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground mt-12 mb-4">Banks That Accept ITINs</h2>

<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">Several US banks and fintech platforms accept ITINs for non-resident account holders:</p>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Mercury</h3>
<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">Mercury is a popular choice for non-resident LLC owners. They accept ITINs along with your LLC formation documents and EIN.</p>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Relay</h3>
<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">Relay offers business banking for non-residents and accepts ITINs for account verification.</p>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Wise Business</h3>
<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">Wise Business allows you to open a US business account with an ITIN and provides multi-currency features.</p>

<h3 class="text-xl font-semibold text-foreground mt-8 mb-3">Traditional Banks</h3>
<p class="text-muted-foreground leading-relaxed mb-4">Some Chase and Bank of America branches accept ITINs, but requirements vary by location.</p>

<h2 class="text-2xl font-bold text-foreground mt-12 mb-4">Documents You Need</h2>

<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">ITIN assignment letter</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">LLC Articles of Organization</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">EIN confirmation letter</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">Operating Agreement</li>
<li class="ml-6 text-muted-foreground">Valid passport</li>
